script.base: Spread, total, moneyline and line movement were not saved, so this is a form-only script, not the book's expected leader or point total. Both clubs have a clear RB1 over the last 3 games (J.Love 41 carries/160 yards, C.Skattebo 50/177) and both defenses allow 4.6-plus YPC (NYG 4.94, ARI 4.63), so the base lean is both backs stay involved rather than a pass-only game we cannot confirm. The pass split is the edge: NYG has allowed only 6 passes of 20-plus yards on 101 attempts and about 6.7 YPA outside, so ARI's completed yards should stay with T.McBride (34 targets, 211 yards, 5.4 air yards per target) rather than M.Harrison's deep air (159 air yards on 9 targets); ARI's pass defense is the leak (9.0-plus YPA in every zone, 9 explosives on 84 attempts) if NYG is neutral or trailing.
script.flip1: If the unknown leader jumps ahead early, the trailer abandons the run: Love (13.7 carries/game) or Skattebo (16.7) rush yards stall and pass attempts rise. That flip helps McBride only if ARI is the trailer; if ARI leads and leans on Love (41 carries), McBride's target floor is the thing that breaks.
script.flip2: If NYG's 26% blitz gets home, ARI QB EPA flips from +0.18 with no blitz to -0.12 vs blitz (n=28), Harrison/Wilson deep yards die, and checkdowns toward McBride (and Love, 12 targets) rise — McBride over survives this flip and the Harrison under is helped by it. The other flip is ARI blitzing above its 22% rate: NYG QB EPA is -0.62 vs blitz (n=29) vs +0.28 clean, which would kill NYG pass-catcher overs we are not betting.

NYG's usage king C.Skattebo (50 carries, 3.54 YPC) overlaps ARI's soft run defense (4.63 YPC, 11 runs of 10-plus), but his rush line 62.5 sits above his own 59.0 yards/game, so that overlap is not a priced leg.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and McBride stayed under 63.5 while Harrison cleared 34.5. The middle bleed was 9 attempts at 8.11 YPA, too small to be a matchup, and NYG's real pass defense (6.72 and 6.69 YPA on 91 outside attempts, 6 explosives on 101 throws) shortened McBride once the 26% blitz turned his 5.4-aDOT routes into low-YAC checkdowns without adding the 11th target. Harrison already has 159 air yards on 9 targets and 8.1 yards per target when thrown to, so one of the roughly two explosives NYG allows per game, or a bump from 3 targets to 5, puts him over 34.5 by itself. No spread means an ARI-trailing script we could not see would aim those deep shots at him, and a McBride limitation missing from the injury report would kill the over without ever showing up in the L3 usage. That tail is why both are leans; the median path (McBride's 70.3 on a stable 34-target role, Harrison's 24.3 on 9 targets into a 5.9% explosive defense) is still the stronger case.
slip_story: One script: NYG suppresses explosives (6/101) and ARI's completed passing value stays with the primary intermediate target, especially if the 26% blitz pushes ARI QB EPA negative. Stack McBride recyds over 63.5 with Harrison recyds under 34.5. Do not add Wilson or Harrison overs, do not add Skattebo or Love rush overs (own rates sit under those lines), no game total (not saved), no TD legs, one market per player. Both legs fail together only if ARI leads big and stops throwing while still sneaking Harrison one explosive.
